reading.body:
Oregon's 2026 legislative record contains 15 bills, but only two mention artificial intelligence directly, and none are lawsuits.

The two AI-titled bills are SB1546, on artificial intelligence companions, and HB4103, on artificial intelligence. The other 13 cover state financial administration, elections, affordable housing, batteries, data brokers, economic development, public safety, medical assistance, semi-independent agencies, journalism compensation, downcoding, and a memorial resolution. None of those titles indicate AI, compute, or data center infrastructure.

For AI scaling, this list shows no Oregon legislation on power generation, transmission, or data center construction. The battery bill HB4144 is the closest to energy policy, but its title does not tie it to AI or compute. The data also contains no lawsuits, so it cannot support conclusions about litigation in Oregon.
